exposure: parents' perception of breast milk (measured by 'adult's perception level of breast milk scale')
mother's history of breastfeeding a previous child for >=6 months
outcome: exclusive breastfeeding status in the first 6 months
adult's perception level of breast milk scale scores
cohort: Parents of healthy, term infants born between July 1 and September 30, 2018, initially including 341 families and followed longitudinally.
finding: There was no correlation between parents' breast milk perception levels and exclusive breastfeeding status in the first 6 months, although previous breastfeeding experience and pacifier/baby bottle use were associated with exclusive breastfeeding.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was related to breast milk perception levels, with mothers who had a cesarean section having lower perception scores, while fathers whose spouse had a cesarean section had higher scores compared to normal delivery.
